regime_context: The detector shows Banks (H + HK) as the dominant, trend-eligible leader with crowded positioning and weak breadth (0.769), while Energy (H-shares) is the closest eligible challenger with better breadth/trend-health and no crowding — a narrow (24% eligible), non-directional rotation with no one-narrative dominance. Cross-sectional momentum rank here is an attention lens, not alpha; the only validated leg is absolute-trend gating, so any lean is a durability/risk-discipline call, not a momentum prediction.
emerging_watch: Watching whether the rotation margin (Banks vs Energy, currently 0.41) narrows below ~0.15 AND Energy's breadth stays above Banks' — that would be a confirmed handoff signal, not a prediction; until then the Banks lead is intact and I am not fading it.

theses.subject: Banks (H + HK)
theses.thesis: Banks lead the eligible trend-gated set and show modest absolute-trend eligibility, so a trend-following risk-discipline stance is reasonable. But crowdedness (z 1.06) and only mixed breadth argue this is a cap-not-chase situation; the marginal durability bar of 0.68 is not exceptional. Lean overweight ONLY because the trend gate validates staying-power control — not because rank 1 predicts return.
evidence: crowding_z 1.06, crowded=true (size-down caution, not a fade)
rotation leader with margin 0.41 over Energy
theses.dissent: Crowded positioning with only mixed trend-health and weak cohesion (one_narrative=false) means this leadership may chop rather than compound; the rank-1 spot is coincident attention, not evidence of forward return.

falsifier.text: Banks (H + HK) loses its eligible=true trend-gate status before the 20-day check-by, or breadth drops below ~0.6 while score slips under Energy's.

check.reason: theme has no scalar etf_proxy → not cleanly scorable

theses.subject: Energy (H-shares)
theses.thesis: Energy has the cleanest trend health of the eligible set — durability_bar 0.8, hurst_tag trend, breadth 0.8, and no crowding (z 0.32). As a trend-discipline candidate it is the most internally coherent eligible theme. Its slightly lower cross-sectional score vs Banks is not a forecast difference; the coherent trend leg is what matters. Lean overweight as the less-crowded, higher-quality trend alternative within the top group.
theses.dissent: Energy is commodity-linked and can re-rate sharply on macro/oil shocks; its H-share complexion ties it to flows that can reverse independent of the trend leg. Higher trend quality does not imply higher forward return — cross-sectional rank claims no edge.

falsifier.text: Energy (H-shares) durability_bar falls below ~0.6 and hurst_tag flips off trend, or it loses eligible=true while Banks holds; any pullback of breadth below 0.6 before the 25-day check-by.

check.reason: theme has no scalar etf_proxy → not cleanly scorable
